title: 4.9 LEVELIZED COST OF ENTRY
summary: LCOE analysis is presented as a way to gauge whether long-term power prices sit near a fundamental equilibrium, since new generation only gets built when expected prices clear the cost of entry. The chapter breaks down how that break-even cost is actually assembled — spreading the cost of new entry over an asset's life using discounted cash flow, with the weighted average cost of capital and capital recovery factor converting that stream into a levelized figure. It also notes that this framework isn't limited to long-horizon forecasting alone but shows up in a range of other commercial and regulatory uses.
